bottleneck: Cystic fibrosis gene therapy must reach airway epithelial cells through thick, infected mucus that traps vectors, while mucociliary clearance sweeps them away before transduction. Repeated dosing — needed because airway cells turn over — is blocked by anti-vector immunity after the first exposure. Decades of trials have failed to achieve durable CFTR expression in the lung despite success in other organs, making CF the canonical example of a delivery barrier defeating a solved biology.
current_state: CFTR modulators help most patients, but gene therapy for the lung remains stalled. Aerosolized vectors and LNPs are in early trials with modest results and no durable correction yet.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Medicine: Precision Delivery

title: Lung mucus barrier defeats cystic fibrosis gene therapy
why_it_blocks: The lung's defenses evolved to keep particles out — including therapeutic ones. Until vectors can penetrate mucus and survive clearance, CF gene therapy stays a decades-old unfulfilled promise for patients modulators cannot help.
